(Cambodia): .The USAID Greening Prey Lang activity works to protect Cambodia's largest designated conservation area and help the local people who depend on it for their livelihoods. The activity improves forest management, promotes resilient and low-emissions development, and advocates for improved governance of the Prey Lang extended landscape. The activity provides technical assistance for sustainable landscape management and biodiversity conservation to beneficiaries who depend on the area's ecological services, such as water, biodiversity, and food. It works to increase the capacity of relevant stakeholders to assess and address sustainable landscape issues. In addition, this activity supports community-based organizations, private sector, and other stakeholders to better manage Protected Areas and Community Forests to ultimately reduce environmental crimes, such as land encroachment, illegal logging, and wildlife poaching. In addition, the activity improves market linkages for non-timber forest products and eco-tourism...The activity falls under the Administration's priority to promote climate security and resilience, modernize information, and champion equity and inclusion for all. The activity also supports the Indo-Pacific Framework and contributes to Mission Objective 1 (CDCS DO1) "Inclusive and Sustainable Economic Growth Broadened.".

description.narrative: (Cambodia): Rapid degradation of forests due to a systemic failure of natural resource management and governance are undermining the political stability, economic health, and climate resilience of Cambodia. The Wildlife Sanctuary Support Program works to improve biodiversity conservation and ecosystem health; increases sustainable economic opportunities; and strengthens landscape governance in two wildlife sanctuaries in Mondulkiri province. The activity builds the capacity of local communities and coordinates with Royal Government of Cambodia technical officers to better manage natural resources; supports the analyses and implementation of spatial plans to balance economic development while maintaining the ecological sanctuary's integrity; and, promotes alternative livelihood opportunities to reduce the dependence on the timber and non-timber forest products. The activity supports the Administration priority of ensuring effectiveness and accountability to the American taxpayer by using evidence to inform budget, program planning, and management decisions. The activity also supports the Administration priority of building self-reliance by increasing engagement with local partners to strengthen their ability to implement their own development agenda. In addition, the activity contributes to Mission Objective 4.2 (CDCS DO3) - Strengthen sustainable and resilient pathways out of poverty. The activity was awarded through a sole source mechanism to an implementing partner with unique qualifications to carry out the work. The award was made in accordance with federal procurement regulations.

title.narrative: USAID Keo Seima Conservation Project (former: Eastern Plains Landscape)

description.narrative: (Cambodia): Keo Seima Wildlife Sanctuary (KSWS) is a biologically and culturally rich protected area on a deforestation frontier, and a habitat of globally significant populations of endangered primates and elephants. KSWS is also the traditional home of the Bunong indigenous group. In the past ten years, KSWS's rich and diverse forests have experienced rapid population growth facilitated by road improvement and incentivized by the spread of agro-industrial concessions which strains natural resources. The activity will improve the transparency and effectiveness of law enforcement to protect forests and biodiversity using Spatial Monitoring And Reporting Tool technology; monitor wildlife populations and forest cover to ensure evidence-based management decisions; increase economic opportunities for indigenous and marginalized people by increasing market linkages, and equitable benefit sharing from sustainable financing such as carbon stock sales; empower indigenous communities and marginalized people to gain secure land tenure and rights to forest resources; and, create a communications strategy to influence decision-making for sustainable use and management of natural resources. The activity supports Administration priorities to align with U.S. National Security objectives by increasing the transparency and effectiveness of law enforcement to combat wildlife trafficking, poaching and illegal timber exports. Further, the activity contributes to Mission Objective 4.2 (CDCS DO3) - Strengthen sustainable and resilient pathways out of poverty. The activity was awarded through a sole source mechanism to an implementing partner with unique qualifications to carry out the work, in accordance with federal procurement regulations. ....

(Cambodia): Promoting Healthy Behaviors (PHB) improves healthy behaviors for Cambodians by reducing barriers to behavior change, both cross-cutting and specific to family planning; tuberculosis; malaria; maternal and child health; nutrition; water, and hygiene. .PHB delivers technical assistance to develop and implement targeted Social Behavior Change (SBC) activities. PHB supports a mass media campaign targeting adolescents and women of reproductive age to address family planning myths and misconceptions, and promote accurate information about modern contraceptive methods. PHB disseminates messages on TB symptoms and treatment adherence, antenatal and postnatal care with nutrition, and non communicable disease health education. PHB will expand malaria health education activities by using tools and materials developed in FY 2021 to cover additional villages in targeted provinces. PHB supports the National Programs for development of SBC guidelines, tools and other health education materials through digital technology, and provides the capacity building to program technical staff on how to implement the SBC work. PHB will expand the perception of health care campaigns through social media platforms and community health education work to improve early and appropriate health seeking behaviors that would benefit the overall health system of Cambodia. .The activity falls under the administration's "Advancing global health security, and mitigating development and humanitarian impacts" priority through improving the health behaviors of Cambodians. In addition, the activity contributes to USAID/Cambodia's CDCS 2020-2025 DO 2, "Health, education, and welfare of Cambodians improved through enhanced services" by improving health behaviors ensuring Cambodians seek and receive quality healthcare without financial hardship. This activity supports the ICS MO 2.3, Sub 2.3.1, "By 2024, quality of and access to priority health services improved."

Areas of capacity development may include, but are not limited to, technical expertise (e.g., democracy, legal reform, standards of care); CSO self-regulation (e.g., establishing CSO Codes of Conduct); organizational capacity (e.g., strategic planning, financial management and accountability, public relations and outreach, revenue generation, accountable fundraising, constituency relations, member services, relationship management, learning and adaptation); and advocacy training.

(Cambodia): Enhancing Quality of Healthcare Activity (EQHA) will improve the quality of public and private health facilities to develop and implement patient-centered quality improvement (QI) plans. With FY 2021 funds, EQHA will institutionalize QI approaches within the sub-national health system by increasing local management and ownership, integrating disease-specific QI needs into the routine public health assessment system, and strengthening a national performance-based incentive program. EQHA will work with the public and private sector to improve modern contraceptive use, tuberculosis case detection, and HIV/AIDS integration. EQHA will partner with health professional associations and councils to promote a continuing professional development system to strengthen regulation and licensing reform efforts and will support the implementation of the new management of health services law that includes an accreditation system. EQHA will work with health training institutions to reform training methodologies to produce better-trained healthcare providers. EQHA will continue to build on its quality improvement platform to improve the Cambodian health system's preparation, detection, and response to COVID-19 community transmission in Cambodia..EQHA supports the Administration's priorities to enhance U.S. leadership in responding to the disruption and suffering caused by the global COVID-19 pandemic. EQHA will also support the development and application of information technology platforms, data, and tools to support health workforce capacity, promote e-referral systems, and foster transparent and accountable healthcare systems to respond to citizens' needs. EQHA contributes to USAID/Cambodia's CDCS 2020-2025 Development Objective 2, "Health, Education, and Welfare of Cambodians Improved Through Enhanced Services.".

title.narrative: Cambodia Rural Sanitation Development Impact Bond (DIB)

description.narrative: (Cambodia): .With FY2021 funds, the Cambodia Rural Sanitation DIB activity will leverage the private sector and other stakeholders to support food insecure communities and vulnerable populations to improve access to affordable and sustainable water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) products and services. The activity will promote market-sustained and integrated sanitation services, including strengthening the ability of local business owners to provide sanitation products and services, safe fecal sludge management, and better integration of sanitation with handwashing and clean water solutions. The activity will reach 85 percent rural sanitation coverage by 2023 in 1,600 villages declared Open Defecation Free across six provinces. description.narrative: (Cambodia): The Innovations for Social Accountability in Cambodia (ISAC) activity expands citizen participation and engagement to hold local governments accountable for public services (e.g., health, education, administrative and other services) through improved access to credible information, increased engagement and dialogue of citizens with their local officials, and the application of social media and technologies to increase transparency, accountability, and governance. ISAC also enhances independent media through the creation of a safe digital platform for reporting on government performance, supports existing independent media outlets, and trains citizen journalists as content creators and data curators. ..FHI 360 implements ISAC. USAID awarded ISAC through a competitive process in which the offeror with the best value to the U.S. government was selected, in accordance with federal procurement regulations...By empowering citizens to improve health, education, and administrative services through social accountability interventions, ISAC supports USAID/Cambodia's CDCS 2020-2025 Development Objective 3, "Human rights protected and government accountability advanced". In addition, this activity supports the ICS Mission Objective 3.2, sub-objective 3.2.2, "by 2024, civic participation, action for reforms, and public oversight of government institutions (particularly at the grassroots) strengthened". It also supports the Indo-Pacific Strategy Goal 1: "Advance a free and open Indo-Pacific". ISAC supports multiple administration's priorities, including 1) Upholding universal values and promoting human dignity; 2) Renewing and championing democracy and human rights, promoting transparent and accountable systems responsive to their citizens, and addressing disinformation; and 3) Championing equity and inclusion for all, to counter discrimination and social inequity.....

USAID awarded this contract through a competitive process in which the offeror with the best value to the U.S. government was selected..The activity falls under the administration's priority of "advancing global health security as well as detecting, preventing, controlling, and treating disease and pandemics." In addition, this activity supports the ICS Mission Objective 2.3, Sub-objective 2.3.1, "By 2024, quality of and access to priority health services improved." It also supports the Indo-Pacific Strategy Goal 2: "Build connections within and beyond the region." The activity supports the FY 2022 - 2026 State-USAID Joint Strategy Plan Strategic Objective 1.1, "Leadership in strengthening global health security" and aligns with the East Asia Joint Regional Strategy's Objective 2.1, "Build sustainable and resilient health systems to detect and respond to emerging challenges, including current and future pandemics". This activity is included in the FY 2022 Malaria Operational Plan and is fully aligned with the PMI goals... ...

title.narrative: USAID Digital Workforce Development (formerly USAID Digital Future Cambodia )

description.narrative: (Cambodia): .The USAID Digital Future Cambodia activity aims to create a cohort of Cambodian youth with enterprise-driven skills, training, and qualifications that will help them contribute to Cambodian society and succeed in a modern digital economy. The activity will also support an open internet and freedom of information exchange in order to encourage competition, innovation, and promote international standards for information technology (IT) certification and advance Cambodia's economic diversification in the digital age. FY 2021 funds will be used to strengthen targeted IT certifications, short-courses, non-degree programs, and bachelor's degrees offered by Cambodian higher education institutions (HEIs), build capacity of HEI faculty to prepare them to meet accreditation standards, and increase scholarship, internship, and networking opportunities to support practical skill-building and linkages to job opportunities for Cambodian youth...The activity supports all USAID/Cambodia's CDCS 2020-2025 Development Objectives by promoting internet freedom of information exchange, empowering youth through education and enterprise-driven job skills, and supporting sustainable economic livelihoods through market-based solutions. The activity will contribute to U.S. foreign policy priorities in the Indo-Pacific region by building partnerships between U.S. and Cambodian universities and expanding digital access, thus reducing malign regional influence and supporting growing economic opportunities and prosperity for Cambodians and Americans. The activity will also support multiple priorities of the Administration, including 1) Renewing and championing democracy and human rights; 2) Building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workforce; and 3) Modernizing IT, data, and mobility. The activity will be competitively awarded based on the best value to the U.S. government, in accordance with federal procurement regulations..

description.narrative: (Cambodia): .The Morodok Baitang activity fosters sustainable, conservation-friendly, climate-smart, and socially equitable economic growth for Cambodians. The activity supports strategic partnerships between rural communities, private sector actors, and their development partners to increase revenues and employment opportunities; and to accelerate economic diversification to improve livelihoods, attract investment, and create jobs. ..Morodok Baitang builds on prior and current USAID investments in biodiversity conservation, low emissions development, improved livelihoods for natural resource-dependent communities, and natural resource governance, but has a stronger focus on improving conditions for private sector investment and sustainability of USAID's efforts. USAID awarded the activity to Tetra Tech ARD and three sub-contractors including Wildlife Conservation Society, Dalberg, and Mekong Strategic Partners, through a competitive process in which the offeror with the best value to the U.S. government was selected, in accordance with federal procurement regulations. .The activity falls under the administration's "Promoting net-zero, climate-resilient future" priority by working with relevant stakeholders to promote technology that enhance community resilience and contribute to low emission development. The activity contributes to achieving USAID/Cambodia's CDCS 2020-2025 Development Objective 1, "Inclusive and sustainable economic growth broadened" and the ICS Mission Objective 2.1, Sub-objective 2.1.2, "By 2024, civil society and private sector actors have improved management of and sustainable and accountable development practices on two million hectares of biodiverse and biologically significant areas" through interventions that conserve Cambodia's unique biodiversity and improve accountable and equitable economic development.... .

title.narrative: Feed the Future Cambodia Harvest III

description.narrative: (Cambodia): .The Feed the Future Cambodia Harvest III activity promotes sustainable, broad-based economic growth through increased diversification and competitiveness in Cambodia's agriculture sector. Through private sector engagement within key agriculture market systems, the activity creates jobs, increases livelihoods, and improves diets and well-being for Cambodians, especially women, youth, and marginalized populations. The activity provides targeted demand-driven support to agricultural cooperatives, farmer associations, market actors, financial institutions, and/or micro, small and medium enterprises investing to take advantage of domestic, regional, and international market opportunities. Furthermore, the activity also engages the private sector in activities that focus on integrating climate-smart agriculture approaches and solar green energy to increase food security and reduce the vulnerability of production loss from climate stress...The activity is exploring partnership opportunities with U.S. firms to expand market access and sourcing requirements including the possibility of U.S.-Cambodian joint ventures that can contribute to developing a skilled workforce and increase job creation in the United States and Cambodia. Abt Associates Inc implements the activity and USAID awarded this activity through a competitive process in which the offeror with the best value to the U.S. government was selected, in accordance with federal procurement regulations..The activity supports the administration's "Growing economic opportunities" priority, specifically in agriculture by promoting improved supply chains, leveraging private sector partnerships, and supporting climate-smart agriculture technologies. This activity contributes to achieving USAID/Cambodia's CDCS 2020-2025 DO1, "Inclusive and sustainable economic growth broadened" by promoting market-based trade and competitiveness within the agriculture sector supporting IPS.

DC-Cam is an independent research institute that has its origins in the Cambodian Genocide Program created at Yale University in 1994 with a grant from the U.S. Department of State. DC-Cam aims to serve as a permanent resource providing the public with a better historical understanding of the Khmer Rouge regime. It also serves as a resource for Cambodians and others who may wish to pursue legal redress for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity perpetrated under the Democratic Kampuchea regime from 1975-79. DC-Cam catalogues public documents; interviews former Khmer Rouge functionaries; maps mass graves; produces the magazine Searching for the Truth; maintains a library, audio-visual studios, printing house and exhibition hall; manages a training institute; and provides psycho-social assistance to those victims who suffered torture under the Khmer Rouge regime through the Victims of Torture Project.

description.narrative: The Improved Basic Education in Cambodia Project has been designed with the goal of promoting better educated youth with increased access to a quality and relevant basic education. The development hypothesis underlying the project's technical approach is that in order to increase access to a high quality, relevant education, one must simultaneously address a myriad of both demand and supply-side factors in a way that empowers local stakeholders and builds ownership. These factors are often linked and vary according to local context. Therefore, programming must take a holistic approach that is flexible enough to respond to evolving needs identified by stakeholders at the local level as well as within the national policy context.

description.narrative: (Cambodia): The Counter-Trafficking in Persons II program focuses on protection, prevention, prosecution, and partnership to improve the ability of the Cambodian government and civil society to reduce human trafficking and exploitation. The Mission is conducting a mid-term evaluation of this project and will incorporate the recommendations from the evaluation to improve its interventions. FY 2014 interventions will provide direct support to trafficking survivors, improve the standards of care for shelters, and train local police on victim identification. The project will also provide legal aid to survivors, partner with recruitment companies to educate migrant workers on safe migration, and assist the Ministry of Labor on tracking migrant worker complaints.

description.narrative: (Cambodia): The Social Health Protection project continues to provide technical assistance to the Ministry of Health (MOH) to strengthen the social health insurance program for the poor, known as the Health Equity Fund (HEF). This fund pays for quality and life-saving health services for the poor. FY 2017 funds will support MOH and the government of Cambodia to develop the Payment Certification Agency (PCA) as the semi-autonomous government institution to take over management and funding responsibilities of HEF. The project involves civil society and communities in making transparent the poor identification process for receiving HEF benefits and in providing feedback on service quality. FY 2017 funds will also support revision of the HEF benefit package to expand its coverage to vulnerable populations, including people living with HIV/AIDS and TB patients. USG support will enable the government of Cambodia to provide HEF coverage to over three million poor and vulnerable Cambodians.

(Cambodia): The Quality Health Services (QHS) project will improve quality of services in public-sector clinics and hospitals, to improve maternal, neonatal and child healthcare in nine focus provinces. With FY 2017 funds, the QHS project will continue to provide on-site coaching to health providers on newborn care and basic and emergency obstetric care (including prevention and treatment of postpartum hemorrhage, pre-eclampsia and eclampsia). QHS will improve the skills of healthcare providers to screen and treat severe acute malnutrition according to national standards. QHS will also train healthcare providers to identify and treat nutrition-related issues and pediatric TB and improve infection control in public-sector facilities. The project will reach up to 600 facilities and serve nearly six million people. In FY 2017, QHS will begin transitioning its intervention to the host government.

(Cambodia): The Health Information, Policy, and Advocacy (HIPA) project will improve the quality and use of population and health data reported within the Cambodian government's health information system and vital statistics registration database. The refinement of the health information system will improve the accuracy and quality of reported data from both public and private health care providers. In FY 2016, activities will introduce a new user-friendly dashboard for use by health and non-health authorities to improve the planning and allocation of resources for health priorities at all level. HIPA will pilot an electronic tuberculosis (TB) information system to increase the efficiency of reporting TB data and linking it to the overall health information system. With FY 2018 funds, NOURISH will advocate for policy changes using evidence from the field. ..NOURISH will also intensify implementation of nutrition and WASH activities in low coverage villages, where it will support community nutrition services, including growth monitoring and promotion; promotion of better feeding practices for infants and young children through social behavior change communication; and, conditional cash transfers. NOURISH will support target villages, amongst the poorest, to become open defecation free by conducting community-led total sanitation activities. The activity will promote the production and use of a fish preservative as a food additive for children under five and the planting of nutritious vegetables in home gardens, especially for the landless poor. description.narrative: (Cambodia): Data indicate that many young Cambodians are engaging in high-risk sexual behavior without contraceptive protection, resulting in unwanted pregnancies and infections. In response, the U.S. government will fund a communications campaign to promote and increase young Cambodians' knowledge of positive social norms on gender and sexual and reproductive health. The campaign will target youth between the ages of 15 and 24 years of age. The project will also include a call-in center that will provide youth with information and advice about their sexual health. This multi-media health project will develop and air a drama series on television, radio, and the internet to encourage safe sexual practices that prevent unwanted pregnancies and reduce the transmission of infections. The campaign is expected to reach more than one million Cambodian youth.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Cambodia Rice Field Fisheries II

description.narrative: Rice field fisheries (RFF), defined as the fishing done in and around rice fields, particularly during the flood season, are a vital source of income and nutrition for Cambodias poor farmers. To increase productivity and maintain biodiversity of wild fish in RFF, the project works in the Tonle Sap floodplain to improve management of community fish refuges (CFR), which provide dry season sanctuaries for broodstock. Building on phase I, the project focuses on replicating and scaling up best practices for CFR management, including efficient water use and integration with food crops, and promoting the nutritional benefits of consuming fish.

Increase the availability and use of proven life-saving interventions that address the major killers of mothers and children and improve their health and nutrition status, including effective maternity care and management of obstetric complications; prevention services including newborn care, routine immunization, polio eradication, safe water and hygiene, and micronutrients; improved maternal, infant and young child feeding; and treatment of life-threatening childhood illnesses.
